subject: Dedicated capacity handoff: GPU comparison + validation runbook
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@stratomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity handoff + validation plan

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum going.

Call highlights (from our side):
- StratoMed target SLOs: non-streaming P99 <= 350 ms, streaming partials P95 <= 200 ms; target sustained throughput around 150 req/s with bursts to 220 req/s.
- Typical prompt profile: median 110 tokens in, 220 tokens generated (avg 330 tokens round-trip); ~70% of requests use streaming partials.
- Data residency: US-east, private Dedicated pool; compliance questions to follow with your security team.

Proposed performance validation plan (high level):
1) Baseline perf run: dry-run on hosted model variant to confirm token distribution (we'll align on prompt corpus).
2) GPU matrix: run dedicated validation on 3 candidate configs (A100 40GB multi-instance, H100 80GB single-instance, L4x2 with quantized weights) to measure P50/P95/P99, tail stalls, and KV cache behavior.
3) Throughput sweep: incremental concurrency from 8 -> 128 to identify saturation point and recommended reserved throughput.
4) Streaming stress: reproduce your 70% streaming traffic mix and measure partial latency and jitter.
5) Safety/rollback: define automatic fallback to compatible model variant under capacity pressure.

Requests from you for the validation run:
- Can you share a 200–500 sample prompt set (anonymized) that represents steady-state mix?
- Any hard constraints on cold-starts or startup time for warm pools?

Attachments: StratoMed-SLO-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet for you to fill), redwood-dedicated-runbook-v1.pdf (our proposed test templates).

If this looks good I'll loop in Karthik to schedule the validation window and Ben for commercial sizing. Proposed timeline: baseline next week (week of 11/16) -> matrix runs the week of 11/23.

Thanks — Avery

From: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@stratomed.com>

Cc: Priya Sen <priya.s@stratomed.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity handoff + validation plan

Avery — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:

1) SLO nuance: P99 <= 350 ms applies to single-turn interactive queries (no function calls). For multi-step workflows (callbacks, tooling) we accept P99 <= 600 ms but want stable streaming partials for UX.
2) Token budget: our current cost target is equivalent to <$0.02 per 1k output tokens after infrastructure — happy to discuss tradeoffs but want to keep the per-token infra spend predictable.
3) Warm pool: we need warm cold-starts within 120s for burst scaling (customer SLAs).

We'll provide an anonymized 300-sample prompt set by EOD tomorrow (11/12). Also attaching our internal perf baseline (.csv) from a short experiment — it shows 95th around 280 ms on a 1xA100 config but with high variance at P99.

One ask: can you include a short table with expected reserved throughput per GPU type (e.g., 1xH100 -> X rps sustained at our payload) in the runbook? That will help our procurement team size budget.

Thanks — Daniel
Daniel Reed
Head of Product Engineering, StratoMed
daniel.reed@stratomed.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@stratomed.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity handoff + validation plan

Looping in a quick technical note based on Daniel's baseline and the prompt profile you shared. High-level guidance we propose to test (we'll measure exact numbers during validation):

- Candidate GPU configs to include in the matrix:
  * 1x H100 80GB (single-instance, best tail latency for long-context workloads)
  * 2x A100 40GB (multi-instance / sharded pools, good throughput for batched workloads)
  * 4x L4 / L40-like (quantized runtime) as a cost-optimized baseline for lighter models and bursty traffic

- Reserved throughput heuristics (estimations before run):
  * H100: ~120-170 rps sustained for 330-token roundtrip at P95 <= 250ms (depends on batching efficiency)
  * 2x A100 (40GB): ~180-260 rps sustained, better tail under batching but watch KV-cache pressure on long contexts
  * L4 cluster: ~80-140 rps sustained, much cheaper but P99 will be higher; good as fallback for non-critical traffic

- Streaming considerations: H100 shows lower jitter on partials; A100 with continuous batching may introduce small interleaving pauses unless we tune micro-batching windows. We should capture partial-latency percentiles during the streaming stress test.

We'll build a short expected-throughput table into the runbook and annotate when numbers are from simulation vs measured. Can confirm schedule once we get the prompt set and your preferred test hours (off-peak vs business hours).

-Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Reed <daniel.reed@stratomed.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity handoff + validation plan

Daniel / Priya — quick commercial note and next steps from procurement side:

- We'll produce an initial sizing recommendation doc after the validation runs. As a bridge, here's a conservative reserve suggestion based on Karthik's matrix: reserve capacity equivalent to 2x A100 40GB for your sustained needs and add a 20% burst buffer (this maps to our Dedicated Bronze tier pricing).
- If the H100 results show better P99 at lower reserved throughput, we can propose a hybrid approach: H100 for low-latency interactive routes + A100 pool for bulk batch/async jobs.
- Pricing: I will attach a preliminary committed-capacity quote and three term options (monthly, annual, 24m committed).

Next steps:
1) Avery to receive prompt set and schedule baseline run (you said EOD 11/12).
2) Karthik to run matrix and upload results into the runbook.
3) Ben to send draft quote post-run (expected by 11/27).

Appreciate the clear objectives — we'll aim for transparency on measured rps per GPU in the final doc.

Thanks — Ben
